answer: During a short voice call the verifier can inject a one-time inaudible watermark tone, and the caller's device must record that tone in the background of its own microphone within five seconds. The watermark is random per call, so a pre-recorded room sample contains the wrong tone or none at all, and a farm would need a live microphone in a distinct sounding room for every simultaneous call. A plume of sound rises and fades too fast to steal, the cipher changes with each call, and a relic of last week's tone is rejected the moment it is checked.
